title: Instrument build-graph, introduce presubmit-condenser and opt-in dep-escort
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Our presubmit lane has grown heavy as we added per-language lint/test shards and dependency scans. That increases feedback latency and CI cost. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) lightweight runtime instrumentation for the repository build graph so we can prioritize hot paths and avoid running expensive checks for low-impact edits; 2) a presubmit-condenser that coalesces fast sanity checks into a compact fastpath and defers expensive/long-running checks to staged lanes; 3) an opt-in CLI 'dep-escort' that authors can run locally to compute a minimal dependency delta and generate a compact shrinkwrap suggestion to reduce noisy dep churn. Summary: - Add build-graph instrumentation (tracepoints + annotation) to ci/graph and build scripts. Instrumentation emits per-target weight and last-run duration metrics to the CI telemetry pipeline (datapoint keys: buildgraph.target_weight, buildgraph.last_duration_ms). - Implement presubmit-condenser in ci/presubmit which detects the change footprint (via build-graph) and routes the PR to one of three fastpaths: tiny (quick lint/spec smoke), focused (language-specific fast tests), and full-stage (deferred deeper tests). The condenser is opt-in via PR label "presubmit:condenser" or auto-enabled for small-footprint edits. - Add dep-escort under tools/dep-escort: a local Python CLI that computes transitive dep deltas, identifies minimal package.json/pyproject updates, and produces a proposed shrinkwrap diff that authors can include. It also annotates the PR with a dependency-signal comment (used by the presubmit-condenser). - Update docs/dev/presubmit.md with workflow and developer guidance. - Split large monolithic CI jobs into smaller tasklets referenced by the new condenser; this reduces warm setup time when only a subset of checks are required. Checklist: [x] build graph proto + metrics emission implemented; [x] presubmit-condenser core routing + label gating; [x] dep-escort CLI with unit tests; [x] docs updated and quickstart added; [x] smaller CI tasklets wired into workflows; [x] end-to-end smoke on main branch. Backwards compatibility: All changes are opt-in by label or controlled by the auto heuristics; existing PRs without labels see the same behaviour unless the auto heuristics consider them "small" edits. Rollout plan: merge to main behind a short feature flag in ci config; enable auto heuristics after 48 hours of telemetry collection and a short opt-out period. Related: ENG-3219 (ci cost reduction), ENG-3220 (dep churn reduction), SUP-1812 (support ticket describing noisy dependency updates).
